chains.title: HOXB13 binding at the enhancer contributes to increased RFX6 expression with T
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, which literature identifies as an rs339331 prostate-cancer risk-associated enhancer involving HOXB13.
chains.cell_type: Prostate cancer context; literature reports HOXB13 involvement at the enhancer, but the supplied evidence does not establish HOXB13 occupancy in LNCaP or VCaP cells.

links.claim: HOXB13 is favored over related homeodomain candidates because its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger in-vitro binding to ref T than alt C, and literature reports increased HOXB13 binding at the region with T. The in-vitro prediction does not establish occupancy.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, and literature places HOXB13 in a transcriptional complex at the rs339331 risk-associated enhancer.

Literature reports that an enhancer-associated GATA2/SMAD4/HOXB13 complex increases RFX6 expression and separately reports increased RFX6 transcription with T. The supplied evidence does not show that HOXB13 alone mediates the expression effect.

The proposed context is prostate cancer, where literature reports the enhancer complex and allele-associated effects. No variant-overlapping HOXB13 peak is reported in the supplied LNCaP or VCaP searches; for VCaP, the evidence does not establish whether a suitable experiment was performed.

The locus is associated with prostate cancer, and literature describes T as the risk allele. The GWAS Catalog lists C as the effect allele but provides no effect direction here, so that record neither confirms nor contradicts the literature's risk-allele direction. The supplied evidence does not establish that the HOXB13-to-RFX6 mechanism causes the risk association.

predictions: In a relevant prostate cancer model, allele-resolved assays should find greater HOXB13 occupancy with T than C, and the T-associated RFX6 expression effect should depend at least partly on HOXB13.

Changing the endogenous allele from T to C should reduce the allele-associated RFX6 effect; HOXB13 perturbation should diminish its HOXB13-dependent component. This differs from an AR-mediated response and from the null.
falsified_if: Adequately sensitive assays in relevant prostate cancer cells find no HOXB13 occupancy at the element and no greater occupancy with T.
Endogenous allele editing produces no reproducible RFX6 change, or the allele-associated RFX6 response persists unchanged after HOXB13 perturbation.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs339331
predictions: The prostate cancer association may reflect linkage to another causal variant, or rs339331 may have no causal TF-mediated allelic effect.
Reported occupancy and enhancer observations may not produce an endogenous TF-dependent change in RFX6 regulation in relevant prostate cells.
falsified_if: Endogenous allele editing reproducibly changes RFX6 regulation in a relevant prostate cancer model, and the effect depends on an implicated TF.

chains.title: AR occupancy may contribute to RFX6 regulation
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, and prostate-tumor literature places it in a reprogrammed AR-binding site.
chains.cell_type: Prostate cancer tumor cells; AR occupancy is reported in literature, but not demonstrated by the supplied matching LNCaP ChIP-seq search.

links.claim: Literature reports greater AR chromatin occupancy with T (ref) than C (alt). The AR-specific QBiC-SELEX model shows no significant effect; the significant result from an NR3C2-mapped model cannot be attributed to AR.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, which literature describes as a reprogrammed AR-binding site in prostate tumors.
RFX6 is prioritized at the locus, and allele-editing literature reports increased RFX6 transcription with T; the supplied evidence does not establish that AR mediates this change.
The proposed context is prostate cancer tumors, where literature reports AR occupancy at the site; the supplied LNCaP search found no AR peak at the variant.

The locus is associated with prostate cancer, but an AR-mediated contribution to risk is unproven. Literature calls T the risk allele; the GWAS Catalog's C effect-allele field has no effect direction in the supplied record.

predictions: Allele-resolved assays in relevant prostate tumors should find greater AR occupancy with T than C if the reported AR mechanism is active.
If AR mediates the RFX6 effect, perturbing AR should reduce or eliminate the variant-associated RFX6 response; this differs from an HOXB13-dependent response.
falsified_if: Sensitive allele-resolved assays in relevant prostate tumors consistently show no greater AR occupancy with T, or show greater occupancy with C.
The variant-associated RFX6 response is unchanged by AR perturbation in an appropriate model.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs339331 resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.

Strinkingly, GATA2 and SMAD4 globally mediated inherited PCa risk and formed a transcriptional complex with HOXB13 at the PCa risk-associated rs339331/6q22 enhancer, leading to increased expression of the PCa susceptibility gene RFX6.
Notable genes of interest include HCP5, RFX6 and H3C1 for risk, and MKI67 and KLF5 for aggressive disease.
